assumptions: All diagrams original qualitative schematics; colours, counts, geometry and positions chosen for teaching. No true three-dimensional section, measured size, activity rate or cell photograph. Rotation changes 2D orientation only.

Representative viable animal epithelial, green mesophyll and typical underground bulb epidermal cells. All three retain nucleus, membrane, cytoplasm, mitochondria and ribosomes; plant profiles include wall and central vacuole. Only this green mesophyll profile includes chloroplasts. Not all cell types follow the profiles.
Mature human red blood cells are an animal exception: no nucleus or mitochondria. A typical animal schematic cannot describe every specialised cell.

CellJobs assumes oxygen, existing sugar, amino acids and other suitable conditions. Mesophyll photosynthesis additionally needs light; no water/CO2 limitation, substrate depletion, temperature or rate simulation. Respiration and protein assembly are possible in these profiles by day and night.

DNA mostly remains in the nucleus; an RNA information copy guides ribosomes. Energy-support arrows are distinct from information and material arrows. Mitochondria perform major aerobic respiration stages; some respiration occurs in cytoplasm. ER/Golgi and many regulation steps omitted.

Tissue diagrams show only representative parts, not a complete leaf section or intestinal wall. Four-level cell/tissue/organ/organism route omits the intermediate organ-system level deliberately without denying it. Stomata belong to epidermis rather than a separate tissue.
Cell structures/function cards reflect biological knowledge, not what an ordinary light micrograph alone establishes. Structural completeness of a notebook is not scientific verification.
